target_name: Van Mossel Voorraad (inventory/stock-count app, Van Mossel Automotive Group)
authorization: Written permission from CEO Rens Boeren (cooby). Scope: voorraad.cooby.nl only. Operator supplied a white-box control copy (source + test DB) run locally for testing.
scope_note: Primary target voorraad.cooby.nl on shared Hostinger VPS 187.77.163.64 (AS47583, Paris FR). Production serves HTTP/2 while the app is Node http.createServer (HTTP/1.1) -> a reverse proxy/TLS terminator sits in front. Sibling cooby.nl apps are OTHER clients - OUT OF SCOPE (confirmed by operator). All dynamic exploit testing performed against a local copy of the exact production code, never against live data.
stack: Node.js 24 single-file backend (app/server.mjs, ~8500 lines, only node: builtins - node:sqlite, node:crypto, node:http). SQLite DB. Vite/React SPA frontend. scrypt password hashing (N=32768). Roles: audit (admin), viewer, scanner. Multi-project model; project_members links users to projects; scanner scan_scope can be projects/cluster/locations.
method: White-box: operator provided controlekopie-2026-10-30.zip (full source + fictitious test DB, 3 seeded accounts). Rebuilt data/inventory.sqlite from database-test.sql, ran app on Node 24 at 127.0.0.1:3080, tested all three roles dynamically plus full source review of auth, authorization, and every /api handler.
defenses_verified_strong: Activation tokens: randomBytes(32) (256-bit), stored only as sha256 token_hash, single-use via atomic consume (UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL), 24h expiry. Not guessable/predictable. T1 CLOSED.
Sessions: randomBytes(32) hex stored as sha256, 12h expiry, HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax (Secure+__Host- on https).
Passwords: scrypt N=32768 r8 p1, verify via timingSafeEqual. 12-char min on activation.
CSRF: /login,/logout,/activeren require Origin===origin AND double-submit token; /api writes require Origin===origin (safeWrite). No bypass.

Authorization/IDOR: projectAccess() + scanScope() + access(roles) enforced on EVERY handler. Empirically: viewer 403 on non-member project /api/data and /api/evidence-export; scanner 403 on /api/import; viewer 403 on /api/manage admin action. T2 CLOSED - no IDOR, no privilege escalation.

No SQLi (fully parameterized prepare/bind; dynamic identifiers hardcoded/whitelisted). No SSRF (fetch targets are server-config OCR URL + fixed RDW endpoint with charset-validated plate). No path traversal (photoPath regex + startsWith(root) guard; static files resolve+startsWith guard).
Client bundle: no hardcoded secrets/keys, no innerHTML/eval/dangerouslySetInnerHTML in app code, strict CSP. No client XSS/secret leak.

findings.title: Login brute-force / rate-limit bypass via X-Forwarded-For spoofing
findings.detail: The only brute-force control is limited(key) keyed on 'login:'+ip+':'+email, threshold 12 per 15 min. The ip is taken from the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header (last value) and only falls back to socket.remoteAddress when XFF is absent. An attacker who sends a changing X-Forwarded-For value gets a fresh counter every request, fully defeating throttling and account lockout. END-TO-END PoC on the exact production code: 40 consecutive wrong-password guesses against a real account with a rotating XFF -> all 401, zero 429; the 41st attempt with the CORRECT password -> 303 success, lockout never engaged. Control test without XFF -> 429 after the threshold. This enables unthrottled credential-stuffing / online guessing against any known employee email (guessable firstname.lastname@). Rises to HIGH if any account uses a weak/breached password. Also explains the earlier live observation of no throttling. PRODUCTION EXPLOITABILITY depends on the front reverse proxy's XFF handling (safe only if it OVERWRITES/APPENDS the real client IP as the last value; unsafe if it passes the client's XFF through) - recommend verifying the proxy config.
findings.fix: Derive client IP only from the trusted proxy (fixed trusted-hop count or a proxy-set header the app controls), never from raw client XFF. Add global and per-account throttling independent of IP, plus progressive delays/CAPTCHA after N failures and breached-password / MFA controls.

findings.title: Evidence-export PDF hash is client-asserted (not server-verified)
findings.detail: evidence-export 'complete' stores pdf_sha256 exactly as sent by the client; the server cannot recompute it because the PDF is rendered client-side. CONFIRMED: the export owner completed an export with a fabricated random pdf_sha256 and the server stored it verbatim (DB value == fabricated hash, status='ready'). For an evidence/audit system the PDF integrity value is therefore a self-attestation. The real integrity anchor (snapshot_sha256 over the actual DB records) IS computed server-side, so data integrity is preserved; only the PDF artifact's integrity claim is unverified. Cross-user completion IS correctly blocked (403).
findings.fix: Document that pdf_sha256 is a client attestation, or render/hash the PDF server-side if it must be authoritative.

findings.title: cooby.nl email auth gaps (no DMARC, SPF ~all)
findings.detail: Domain-level spoofing-adjacent; not the app itself.

findings.title: First-run bootstrap self-provisions audit
findings.detail: On an UNINITIALIZED instance (no settings.campaign), the first authenticated caller of /api/manage action=initialize or /api/location-catalog is created as audit. Not reachable on the configured production environment (campaign already set). Noted for completeness.

earlier_finding_retracted: Prior F1 'no brute-force protection' was a false positive from the live black-box test: rate limiting DOES exist (threshold 12/15min). The live no-throttle observation was an artifact of the egress proxy varying the forwarded IP, which is itself the mechanism behind the real finding (now F1: XFF-based bypass).
dynamic_tests_run: Authorization matrix across all 10 /api endpoints x {unauth,viewer,scanner,audit}: every role-gated route correctly blocks lower roles (verified with valid bodies; empty-body 500s are JSON-parse errors, not authz gaps).
F1 end-to-end: 40 rotating-XFF wrong guesses (0x429) then correct password succeeds -> lockout bypassed. Control without XFF -> 429.
Path traversal: encoded traversal to server.mjs and data/inventory.sqlite via /assets/ all blocked by startsWith(publicDir) guard (404); URL parser also collapses %2e segments.
SQLi: payloads in projectId and login email -> clean 404/401, no SQL errors.
Activation flow: valid token 200, tampered token invalid, pw<12 -> 400, valid activation -> 303, token reuse after consume -> invalid (single-use enforced).
Cross-location photo IDOR: location-restricted scanner gets 200 on allowed location photo, 403 on other-location photo in same project; full-scope scanner 200 (control).
CSRF: /api write with no Origin -> 403, wrong Origin -> 403.
Evidence-export: cross-user completion -> 403; owner completion with fabricated pdf_sha256 -> stored verbatim (F2 confirmed).
minor_observations: Several /api POST handlers return HTTP 500 (generic message, no stack leak) on malformed/empty JSON body instead of 400. Robustness only; informational.
overall_assessment: Well-secured application. Strong, consistently enforced auth/session/CSRF/authorization. One confirmed real finding (F1, medium, XFF rate-limit bypass) plus low/informational items (F2-F5). No IDOR, privilege escalation, SQLi, SSRF, path traversal, client secrets, or XSS found across white-box review + dynamic testing of the exact production code.
pending_decisions: Optional: verify production reverse-proxy XFF handling to confirm F1 exploitability on the live host (vs. the confirmed local PoC).

Operator still offered a fresh activation link / live test accounts - no longer required for core testing since the white-box copy covers it, but useful to validate findings against the live instance if desired.
